q1_issues.issue: The comparative 'warmer' is flattened to the positive property 'warm'; *Comparatives & degree* states a comparative does not entail the positive, so no More/scale atom is emitted and the reified state asserts an unstated positive.
Same flattening at top level: (Member sk_world_1 warm) asserts the world IS warm, which 'feels warmer' does not claim.

(Member sk_friends_1 nearby) predicates a member-level property of the GROUP symbol, which *Categorical statements* explicitly forbids ('a bare (Member <group> <prop>) appears only for a property genuinely of the collection itself'); it should distribute or go on the kind.
The evidential copular verb 'feels' is dropped entirely — no hedge or status atom records that the warmth is how the world SEEMS rather than how it is.

'with friends nearby' is an absolute/circumstantial clause (= 'when friends are nearby'), not a comitative participant or a means, so (With <state> <friends>) records an accompaniment the CoAgent/Instrument split does not sanction and loses the predication 'friends are nearby'.

q2_gaps: comparative with an ELIDED standard ('warmer', no 'than …') — every comparative form in the instruction set requires a second argument, and no encoding is given for the implicit-standard case
evidential / sensory copular verbs ('feels / looks / sounds / smells / tastes ADJ') — only 'seem / appear' with an infinitive are routed (to epistemic status), and only for eventive complements
absolute 'with' clauses (with + NP + predicate) expressing an accompanying circumstance or condition — the 'with'-phrase rule offers only CoAgent vs Instrument
bare-plural argument with an existential (not generic) reading ('with friends nearby') — the determiner rule sends bare plurals to the generic kind
notes: 'With' is an oblique named after its own preposition so it is licensed in form, but the construction it encodes is not one the with-phrase rule covers.
